Day 56 of 100 · Networking Deep Dive

HTTP vs HTTPS

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityNetworking Deep DivePublished artifact recovered

HTTPS is HTTP carried inside a TLS-protected connection, adding confidentiality, integrity and authenticated server identity to the transport path.

Architecture / mental model

HTTP: client ⇄ TCP ⇄ server
HTTPS: client ⇄ TLS over transport ⇄ HTTP messages ⇄ server

How it works

HTTP defines methods, headers, status codes and message bodies. Plain HTTP does not itself protect those messages from network observers or modification.

HTTPS establishes TLS first and then carries the HTTP exchange inside the protected channel. Ports 80 and 443 are common conventions, not the definition of the protocols themselves.

TLS protects the channel. It does not prove the website is ethical, bug-free or safe from application vulnerabilities.

Hands-on reference

curl -v http://example.com
curl -v https://example.com
openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com

Verification

Inspect an HTTP redirect to HTTPS, then validate the certificate/handshake and application response independently.

Field note / gotcha

A valid certificate proves a hostname/trust-chain relationship for the channel, not that the application content deserves trust.

Security considerations

Redirect plaintext HTTP where appropriate, mark sensitive cookies Secure, avoid mixed content and deploy HSTS only after HTTPS works for the intended scope.

What I learned

Encryption changes the trust boundary of the transport path, not the quality of the application behind it.
